exposure: mode of delivery (cesarean, assisted vaginal, spontaneous vaginal)
cohort: The study included 30 patients admitted to the OBGY ward at Vilasrao Deshmukh Government Medical College, Latur, Maharashtra, who underwent emergency peripartum hysterectomy.
finding: The study found that haemorrhagic shock was the most common operative complication (43.33%), with a maternal mortality rate of 3.33% and a neonatal mortality rate of 6.66%.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was the most common mode of birth (53.33%) among patients requiring emergency peripartum hysterectomy.
